name: agent-run-verifier
reason: initial draft, derived from crew.json v1.0

intent.text: A fresh-context subagent that attempts to refute the final green: with every check passing, it audits the map, hunts the false green, and confirms the target and the fence held, so that not-refuted becomes earned evidence rather than absence of doubt.

scope.text: The agent definition: the audit checklist, probing conduct, integrity confirmations, verdict semantics.
Handling harness malfunctions (hook failures, tool crashes, permission misconfiguration); deferred by design.
The content of any template the invoker supplies; templates are project property, referenced by parameter.
Project-specific paths, commands or frameworks; every concrete value arrives via invocation parameters.
The behaviour of any other crew role; collaboration contracts appear here only as this agent's own inputs and outputs.
Judging intent or scope quality; that is the reviewer's reading.

constraints.text: Standard model tier; systematic refutation against known false-green causes.
Fresh context; must not see any implementer or orchestrator reasoning.
Tool policy: read files, run checks and additional probing commands; denied: writing anything.
Failed refutations are reported alongside successful ones; they are what make the green credible.

interfaces.text: Parameters: spec_path, tests_map_path, the merged branch, all check outputs, the diff-boundary result, the test-file change list.
interfaces.name: invocation

interfaces.text: Return contract: refutations as a list of what was tried, what happened, and severity where it succeeded; audit covering map coverage, target integrity and boundary integrity; verdict of refuted | not-refuted with the standing caveat that not-refuted is evidence, not proof.
interfaces.name: return

behaviours.text: Map audit first: every behaviour and edge id is matched to a passing check or an unverified listing; any id in neither state is a finding before any probe runs.
The false-green hunt exercises the feature end to end in at least one way the acceptance script did not, and probes spec-named edges with inputs the tests did not use.
Target integrity: the test-file change list is empty or every change is accounted for, and no check was skipped, quarantined or weakened during the run.
Boundary integrity: the diff-boundary result is clean or every excursion appears in the run's ledger inputs.
The return reports every probe attempted, including those that failed to refute.

edges.text: A probe crashes rather than failing cleanly: reported as a successful refutation of severity high, since the green did not survive contact.
The map lists many deliberately-unverified ids: the audit reports their proportion; a mostly-unverified green is returned as not-refuted with a prominent caveat, not as refuted.
Probing commands are unavailable in the environment: the affected probes are returned as not-run, distinguishing them from failed refutations.

decisions.text: A successful refutation reopens the verify phase and does not merge into the review; the two readings stay independent.
Probe depth beyond one novel end-to-end path and the named edges is left to the invoker's budget.

verification.text: Three layers, in order of trust. Structural: the definition file parses, declares the role's purpose, model tier, isolation, context receives/must-not-see lists, tool allow/deny lists, and an ending that produces the outputs; checked deterministically by a lint script against the crew schema. Scenario: the agent is dry-run against checked-in fixture inputs and its artefacts and returns are asserted deterministically (schema validation, file presence and absence, path boundaries, required fields). Rubric: judgement behaviours that cannot be asserted mechanically are graded from the scenario transcript against this spec's B ids by a fresh grading context. Fixtures and assertions are written before the agent body and locked during runs. Scenario fixtures: a genuinely sound merged fixture; one with a planted unmapped behaviour; one with a weakened test recorded in the change list. Deterministic assertions: return schema-valid; the unmapped id is found in the audit before probes; the weakened test is flagged under target integrity; the sound fixture returns not-refuted with failed refutations listed; no write occurred.

acceptance.text: Structural checks pass; the three fixtures produce the specified audits and verdicts, probes are reported exhaustively, and the merged branch is unchanged by the verification.

open_questions.text: Should the novel end-to-end probe be recorded as a candidate addition to the acceptance script, closing the loop back into the targets?
